result.side_resistance_note: Per-layer side resistance. 'method' gives the mobilized coefficient (alpha=... for cohesive, beta=... for cohesionless, rock socket); 'fs_kPa' is the unit side resistance. effective_top_m/effective_bottom_m reflect the GEC-10 exclusion zones (top 1.5 m or casing depth; bottom 1D in cohesive layers) that carry no side resistance.

result.headline_method: Mobilized toe resistance compatible with the toe penetration
result.neutral_plane_basis: UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 procedure: the load and resistance curves do not intersect with the toe at 100% of its resistance, so the neutral plane is where the pile and the soil settle equally, with the toe force the pile delivers there compatible with the toe penetration it causes (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19; Fellenius 2021). For an end-bearing pile in a stratum stiffer than the compressible soil this is near the top of the bearing layer (§6-7.4 step 5). Unit skin friction (beta layers) and the toe in sand use the final effective stress, sigma'v0 plus the fill / drawdown change (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2). The pile's own weight is left out of the load curve, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 do (include_pile_weight=False).
result.methods_range: The methods give neutral planes from 5.99 m to 18.00 m and drag forces from 226 kN to 969 kN (5 of 7 methods apply).
warnings: The load and resistance curves do not intersect: the toe resistance (2386.7 kN, ultimate unless Nt was given as a mobilized value) exceeds everything the pile can carry to its toe (1369.2 kN with the whole shaft in negative skin friction), so full base mobilization is impossible. The neutral plane is placed where the pile and the soil settle equally, with the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19): 5.99 m, toe force 0.0 kN. Upper bound if the soil settled relative to the pile down to the toe: neutral plane at the toe, drag load 969.2 kN. To intersect the curves instead, give toe_mobilization or Nt for the MOBILIZED toe resistance (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.2: try 0%, 50%, 100%).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at 100% toe mobilization
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves with side and base resistance fully mobilized: UFC §6-7.4 step 3 calls it 'a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'; not conservative for settlement (§6-5.8.4.2).
neutral_plane_comparison.reason: the curves do not intersect: 100% of the toe resistance (2387 kN) exceeds all the pile can deliver to its toe (1369 kN with the whole shaft in negative skin friction).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at 50% toe mobilization
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves, side fully mobilized, toe at 50% of its nominal resistance: UFC §6-5.8.4.2 and GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 analyse 0%, 50% and 100% (Siegel et al. 2013).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at 0% toe mobilization
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves, side fully mobilized, toe at 0% of its nominal resistance: UFC §6-5.8.4.2 and GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 analyse 0%, 50% and 100% (Siegel et al. 2013).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Mobilized toe resistance compatible with the toe penetration
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Pile and soil settle equally at the neutral plane (Fig 6-19). The toe force follows the toe penetration: bearing-stratum compression under the toe force (UFC Eqs 6-51 to 6-54) standing in for a q-z curve, capped at the toe resistance; side fully mobilized.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at the bearing layer (end-bearing pile)
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: UFC §6-7.4 step 5: 'the neutral plane will be located near the interface of the column and the bearing layer for an end-bearing column bearing in a stratum that is much stiffer than the compressible soil'. Plane at the base of the settling soil; set by that statement, not computed.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Neutral plane at the pile toe
neutral_plane_comparison.source: FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.7 (p. 336; Goudreault and Fellenius 1994); CGPR #56 Table 3.1 'end bearing'
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: The whole shaft in negative skin friction: the upper bound on the drag force for a single pile. GEC-12 §7.3.5.7 uses the plane at the toe for group settlement.

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Endo et al. (1969)
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Neutral plane assumed at a fraction of the embedment; an estimate.

result.pile_weight_basis: Pile's own weight left out of the load curve, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 do

notes: Pressure above the excavation: sand apparent envelope (max 31.20 kPa) + surcharge 4.00 kPa (GEC-4 5.2.4 adds surcharge and water explicitly).
The bottom span's load is assigned wholly to the lowest support; free earth support gives that support 72.7 kN/m from the wall below it.
Embedment: free earth support about the lowest support, MR = FS x MD with FS = 1.5 (Caltrans T&S 8-4 uses 1.3).
